subject: Clarify overlapping audit windows & interim attestation options for Q4 renewal
messages:
From: Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@acmecloud.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 timing for renewal — overlapping windows question

Hi Jonas,

Hope you're well. We're in the middle of our renewal cadence with Redwood and hit a timing question on the SOC 2 Type II coverage. Our procurement team is asking for the most recent Type II report and confirmation of coverage through our renewal date (2026-12-31).

Two things came up on our side: 1) the last Redwood Type II covers the period ending 2025-11-30, and 2) our internal audit window overlaps with a planned Redwood Type II next year. Procurement is asking whether a bridge letter or interim attestation is available to cover from the end of the last report to our renewal date.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can provide an interim attestation or bridge letter that references continuous controls coverage through 2026-12-31, or alternatively a plan for providing evidence to satisfy procurement?
- Any timing constraints we should be aware of for DocuSign/PO hold if the attestation is delayed?

I've attached our renewal checklist (see referenced attachments) and copied procurement on the thread.

Thanks,
Sarah
--
Sarah Holt
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Cloud
attachments: renewal_checklist_acme.xlsx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 timing for renewal — overlapping windows question

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear note and the renewal checklist. I pulled this into our procurement/assurance sync. Short answer: we have options, but I want to map them to your procurement milestones so you have a crisp next step.

Summary of options we can offer quickly:
- Interim attestation (short-form letter) that covers control continuity from 2025-12-01 through a target date. This is usually acceptable to procurement teams for contract acceptance.
- A bridge letter plus a commitment to deliver the upcoming Type II report when available (we can give a target month).
- Scoped artifacts: if you need specific control evidence (access logs, change control evidence) we can provide redacted snapshots on a short timeline.

A couple of clarifying questions so we align:
1) Is the procurement/legal team okay with a short-form interim attestation that calls out continuous control operation rather than a formal SOC report?
2) Do you need the attestation notarized or signed by a specific person on our side?
3) What is your PO cutover / invoice hold date in the procurement checklist? If it's before we can deliver the full report, we'll prioritize the interim letter and the minimum artifacts required.

I've attached a draft interim attestation template (Interim_Attestation_Draft.docx) for your review. Laura — can you confirm the internal signatory and approximate delivery timeline for the full Type II? Markus — can you confirm which artifacts we can provide within 5 business days if Acme requests them?

Next step: if Acme is OK with the interim letter, we can finalize it and route to legal & signer within 48 hours.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: Interim_Attestation_Draft.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 timing for renewal — overlapping windows question

Hi all — quick ops note from the assurance side.

1) Signatory: I will sign the interim attestation on behalf of Redwood (Head of Compliance). We typically include the statement that controls were designed and operated during the period specified and call out any exceptions.
2) Bridge vs interim: for procurement where a PO must be released, our short-form interim attestation + two targeted artifacts (a) system access control snapshot and (b) change-control runbook export are usually sufficient.
3) Delivery timeline: if Jonas confirms procurement can accept the attestation by 2026-09-22, we can deliver the signed interim letter on 2026-09-22 and provide the two artifacts within 3 business days thereafter.

Markus — I'll need the access control snapshot and runbook export by EOD 9/17 to hit that schedule.

Sarah — if procurement requires a DocuSign flow or a specific PO hold language, let us know and we'll accommodate.

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@acmecloud.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 timing for renewal — overlapping windows question

Thanks — that timeline works for us. Procurement confirmed they will accept a signed interim attestation plus the two artifacts and will not require a full Type II before PO release. We do need the interim attestation to reference the coverage period through 2026-12-31 and for it to be signed by your Head of Compliance.

Action items we have from this thread:
- Redwood to deliver signed interim attestation referencing continuous control coverage through 2026-12-31 (target: 2026-09-22).
- Redwood to provide access control snapshot and change-control runbook export (target: within 3 business days after 9/22).
- Acme procurement to proceed with PO issuance upon receipt of the attestation + artifacts; we will attach the attestation to the contract file.

Please send the DocuSign link if you want us to sign via that flow; otherwise we can accept a signed PDF.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — will loop legal in the procurement email thread if anything else crops up.

Best,
Sarah
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Cloud
